Subject: Clarify: are partial prompt cache hits billed?

Hi Olga,

Quick follow-up from our procurement review. We're looking at the sample traffic you asked for and have a few questions about how Redwood charges when the model serves from the prefix/prompt cache:

- If a request hits the prefix cache for only the first N tokens (e.g., prompt prefix + system instruction) and the rest is generated, do we get charged for the full output tokens or only the new tokens?
- Does a cache hit from a different session (same account) still count as a hit and avoid charge, or are cache hits scoped per-session/API key?
- Are there volume thresholds where cache hit behavior changes (e.g., beyond commit/tiers)?

Also, we attached the sample CSV you asked for and included the draft rate sheet the procurement team put together. Our finance lead is especially sensitive to any double-billing scenarios.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if easier.

— Maya
Senior Procurement Manager
BrightRetail

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: are partial prompt cache hits billed?

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear questions and the sample. Short answers up front: 1) you are billed only for tokens actually executed by the runtime (we do not charge twice for cached prefixes that fully satisfy a response); 2) cache scope is per-account by default (not per-session) for hosted API; 3) there are no hidden thresholds where behavior flips, but discounts and commit terms can affect effective unit economics.

Details:
- Partial hits: when the prefix cache returns a matching KV prefix and the runtime only needs to generate tokens beyond that prefix, billing is for the generated tokens plus any compute used to confirm the match (the match check is negligible and not metered separately). If your request is fully satisfied from cache (zero new tokens), that request does not accrue output token charges.
- Cross-session hits: hosted accounts share eligible prefix cache entries across API keys under the same account/commit — this is how customers with multi-service deployments benefit. We don’t share cached entries across separate customer accounts.
- Edge cases: if a cached prefix is compatible but requires light post-processing (e.g., format conversion by a post-filter in-host), we meter the new tokens but not the cached portion.

I'll loop in Aditya for the proposed pricing adjustments (since you included a draft rate sheet).

If you want, we can produce an anonymized CSV that converts your sample traffic into estimated monthly bill under (a) no discount, (b) 30% cache-aware discount, (c) 12-month commit pricing. Let me know which scenarios you prefer.

Best,
Olga

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify: billing model + proposal for BrightRetail (cache-sensitive workloads)

Maya — quick pricing note from a product/solutions perspective. We reviewed your sample and sketched two options that are commonly used for cache-heavy customers:

Option A — Cache-Adjusted Usage (recommended for proof-of-value)
- Host: standard per-token posted list price for new tokens.
- Cache credits: for any request where >= 90% of the response is served from cache, we apply a cache credit equal to 75% of the per-output-token charge for that request. Credits are applied monthly against usage.
- No minimum commit.

Option B — Committed Cache Bundle (recommended at scale)
- 12-mo commit with a baseline monthly spend.
- Commit includes a cache uplift: up to X cached-request units per month included at lower effective unit-rate.
- Step-down pricing for additional cached-match volume.

Why not 100% free for cached tokens? Operationally we still allocate short-lived KV memory, and some compute is required to validate matches and rehydrate KV — charging a reduced effective rate aligns costs and discourages gaming the cache.

We can also bake in a clause that stale/mismatched cache entries (where the model would have generated a different token sequence) are not considered hits for credits; we log and surface those during QA.

If BrightRetail prefers the committed option we can run a pro-forma that compares your current projected bill vs. both options.

— Aditya
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — adding a couple practical contract-level clarifications procurement usually asks for:

- Definition of a "cache hit" in the SOW: we will define cache hit as a byte-identical match on the canonicalized prompt prefix used by the model. Include examples in an appendix.
- Auditability: monthly exported report with sample request ids, hit/miss flag, and token accounting (we provide raw logs via secure drop).
- Credits timing: apply credits on the month following usage; credits cannot be carried beyond the 12-mo term unless contractually agreed.
- Protection against accidental over-crediting: we reserve the right to reject credits for synthetic or test traffic if we detect anomalous patterns.

If BrightRetail can commit to a 12-mo baseline we are open to layering in a deeper cache credit (e.g., 90% credit on >=95% cached requests) and an annual true-up.

Will draft language for the appendix and share a short SOW snippet tomorrow.

— Stephanie
